name: Shillong
tagline: Pine hills, waterfalls and Khasi kitchens in the capital of Meghalaya.
intro: Shillong sits at about 1,500 m in the Khasi Hills, cool all year and green after the monsoon. Use it as a base for waterfalls, canyon views and sacred forests a short drive away, and come back each evening for jadoh, live music and the bustle of Police Bazaar.

facts.best_time: October to April for clear views. June to September for waterfalls at full flow, with landslide risk on hill roads.
facts.getting_there: Most visitors fly into Guwahati (about 100 km, 3 hours by road). Shillong Airport at Umroi is about 30 km away with fewer flights.
facts.getting_around: Shared and private taxis; hire a local driver for day trips. Traffic around Police Bazaar is slow at peak hours.
facts.languages: Khasi; English is widely spoken. Hindi is understood in shops and taxis.

emergency.label: Police, fire, ambulance
emergency.note: National emergency number, works from any phone

safety_tips: Fog rolls in fast in the afternoon. Start day trips early and stay back from unfenced edges at viewpoints.
Waterfall steps get very slippery. Wear shoes with grip, especially in the monsoon.
Many shops and restaurants close on Sunday. Plan meals ahead.
Sacred forests have strict local rules: take nothing out, not even a leaf, and go with a village guide.

places.name: Ward's Lake
places.summary: A horseshoe-shaped lake and garden from the British era, a few minutes' walk from Police Bazaar. Walk the paths or feed the fish from the wooden bridge.
tips: Buy puffed rice at the gate to feed the fish.
places.safety: Central and busy during the day.

places.name: Don Bosco Museum
places.summary: Seven floors on the cultures of the North East's many communities: dress, weapons, crafts and homes. Finish on the rooftop skywalk over the city.
tips: Allow two to three hours; it's larger than it looks.

places.name: Elephant Falls
places.summary: A three-tier waterfall in a fern-covered gorge. Steps lead down to each level.
places.best: Morning; the falls are fullest after the monsoon
tips: Combine with Shillong Peak, on the same road.
places.safety: Steps are steep and slippery when wet. Don't climb on the rocks at the base.

places.name: Shillong Peak
places.summary: The highest point near the city, with views over Shillong and the Khasi Hills on a clear day.
places.best: Morning, before the clouds come in
tips: The peak is inside an Indian Air Force area. Carry a photo ID.
places.safety: Follow Air Force rules and don't photograph military installations.

places.name: Umiam Lake (Barapani)
places.summary: A large reservoir framed by pine hills on the road from Guwahati, with boating, kayaking and lakeside viewpoints.

hours.note: Hours shown are for water sports.

tips: Stop here on your way in from Guwahati.
places.safety: Always wear the life jacket. Lake edges are isolated after dark.

places.name: Police Bazaar
places.summary: Shillong's busy shopping and eating hub, with hotels, cafes and street-food stalls around a pedestrian square.

hours.text: Morning to about 20:00; many shops close on Sunday

tips: Try local snacks from the stalls around the square.
places.safety: Crowded and congested. Mind your belongings.

places.name: Laitlum Canyons
places.summary: A ridge where the hills drop away into deep green valleys. A long stairway leads down to Rasong village far below.

fee.indian: Free or a small village fee
fee.foreign: Free or a small village fee

tips: The stairway down is long. Only go down if you're fit for the climb back up.
places.safety: Cliff edges are unfenced and fog arrives quickly. Stay well back from the edge.

places.name: Cathedral of Mary Help of Christians
places.summary: A blue-and-white cathedral on a hill, rebuilt in the 1940s after a fire, with stained glass and terracotta reliefs.
tips: Laitumkhrah's cafes are a short walk away.

places.name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
places.summary: An old-growth forest protected by Khasi tradition for centuries, with monoliths and huge moss-covered trees.
tips: Hire a guide at the village entrance. Walks take one to two hours.
places.safety: Nothing may be taken out of the forest. Stay with your guide on the trail.

food.name: Trattoria
food.known_for: Small, no-frills Khasi kitchen loved by locals: jadoh, dohneiiong and Khasi thalis. Food sells out early.

food.name: Jadoh
food.known_for: Named after the dish: red rice cooked with pork or chicken, plus Khasi sides.

food.name: Iewduh (Bara Bazaar) food stalls
food.known_for: Stalls deep inside Shillong's oldest and largest market. Go in daytime.

food.name: Laitumkhrah street food
food.known_for: Evening momos, smoked-pork noodles and fried snacks.

food.name: City Hut Family Dhaba
food.known_for: Large family restaurant with Indian, Chinese and vegetarian choices.

food.name: Jiva Veg
food.known_for: Pure-vegetarian South and North Indian food.

stays.name: Ri Kynjai – Serenity by the Lake
stays.note: Cottages above Umiam Lake in Khasi style. 30 minutes from the city.

stays.name: Orchid Lake Resort
stays.note: Run by Meghalaya Tourism, on the lake shore.

stays.name: Police Bazaar hotels
stays.note: Walk to everything. Expect noise and traffic.

stays.name: Laitumkhrah guesthouses and hostels
stays.note: Quieter streets with cafes and music bars. Popular with backpackers.
